beats.text: Your PC, {anywhere}from anywhere. Write to it on {telegram}Telegram, to run a {command}command, or to {talk}talk to your assistant.
Let's {connect}connect it, decide {who}who can write to it, and see {use}what it can do.

The easiest way is a {bot}bot of your own. A {guide}guide walks you through it: {botfather}BotFather creates it, you {paste}paste its token into K-Desktop, and {link}link yourself with a code. From then on, the bot {only}only listens to you.

Or use a {account}Telegram account with its own number, best on a phone just for K-Desktop. Unlike the bot, it can {first}write first to its contacts. It needs a free {app}app from Telegram, and its guide explains that too.
Others can write to it too. When {someone}someone new does, you decide: {allow}allow, ignore or block.

Each contact gets a {level}level: {chat}chat only, {commands}chosen commands, {read}tools that only read, {chosen}chosen tools, or {like}like you. And anything that needs confirmation is {asked}always asked to you.
There are {limits}limits, too: messages a minute, and {gaming}only you while you're gaming. In {groups}groups, it answers only when mentioned.
Send {slash}slash commands, and it lists {menu}yours. Tap one, and it {runs}runs on the PC.
Anything else goes to the {assistant}assistant, with its tools. Send a {voice}voice note, and it understands it, and can {answer}answer in its own voice. Send a {photo}photo, and it looks at it.

And the other way round: the {send}Send via Telegram action sends you a text, a {file}file or a {screenshot}screenshot. And the {event}A Telegram message arrives event runs commands from what you send.
One last tip: turn on {notices}important emails in Telegram notices, and the mail that matters {reach}reaches you even away from the PC.
